claims.claim: The confirm has 23 valid cells, 1 unresolved cell and 30 never-started cells; the 31 no-valid-outcome cells are T13=4, T14=9, T15=9 and T16=9. T13-s1-B0-r2 was transport-failed and then successfully retried, so it is one valid cell, not an invalid cell plus an unexecuted one.
claims.harness: immutable manifests, results and reports; Attempt and Unique Cell ledgers
claims.limitation: A correction of the historical merge arithmetic; no new live call and no historical file rewritten.

claims.claim: Six synthetic fixtures distinguish failed-then-valid, failed-unresolved, duplicate-valid, partial-usage, never-started and manifest/cell mismatch; the earliest valid attempt decides a cell and transport-failed attempts never enter the denominator.
claims.harness: 19 assertions over throwaway results/reports
claims.limitation: Synthetic reports; it proves the identity rule, not model behaviour.

claims.claim: Both EF-R2 transport failures are T13/B0. The failed summary of T13-s1-B0-r2 was 75,603 characters and failed in 6 ms; the same cell succeeded on the resume with a 75,603-character summary in 5,858 ms. T13-s2-B0-r1 remains unresolved.
claims.harness: raw request logs and the attempt ledger
claims.limitation: n=2, one local route, no socket identity or keep-alive trace; this is a description, not a provider-level causal estimate.

claims.claim: A local mock server that destroys the socket makes the adapter emit LIVE_TRANSPORT with no usage, and a mid-response reset is never accepted as a silent empty success; partial usage is a valid task outcome with costValid=false.
claims.harness: 13 assertions against a localhost mock; no provider request
claims.limitation: The real proxy is not in the repository; the contract proves classification, not route stability.

claims.claim: The R2 manifest declared rationaleHintTokens 800, but host.mjs did not forward it, so E1 ran the economy preset value 400. The drift affects 18 confirm E1 cells and 6 pilot E1 cells; the forwarded-config preflight passes and would catch a future mismatch.
claims.harness: declared vs effective resolveEfConfig, plus the historical host contract
claims.limitation: The historical cells are not re-run. A 400-pinned completion is comparable to the 23 valid cells; an 800 or shipped-preset run is a different treatment.

claims.claim: Economic admission prices the widest legal span (retain 0) while execution folds the span left after spec.retainTokens. In a 60-case deterministic matrix the median gap was 516, 2,064 and 3,096 tokens at retain 0.04, 0.16 and 0.24; at the default floors no large-span case flipped, and all 3 floor-sensitivity cases flipped admission=true, execution=false.
claims.harness: keyless controlled adapter over the real engine and token meter; 60 default-floor cases plus 3 floor-sensitivity cases
claims.limitation: A keyless matrix, not live model behaviour. The R2 live reports predate the probe, so their exact-span economics is unavailable, not zero.

claims.claim: The opt-in exact-span probe is observational: it records widest/executed spans, estimated and actual checkpoint cost, and the surface delta without changing a verdict, span or exception path; the engine self-test report reconciles actual reclaim with the surface delta.
claims.harness: unit tests plus a scripted E2E self-test
claims.limitation: The probe is off in product deployments and enabled only by the benchmark harness; it measures, it does not fix the admission/execution mismatch.

claims.claim: The current economy, balanced and quality tiers are hypotheses for their effective configs. RC1.3 measured the explicit zero-LLM economy profile (semanticMode: none); the current economy tier adds rationale and system-dedup framing, so that result does not transfer.
claims.harness: TIERS metadata plus resolveEfConfig; 3 tier tests
claims.limitation: Metadata-only correction; no tier value or product default changed. The underlying RC1.3 result remains valid for the profile it measured.

claims.claim: Task outcome, treatment exposure and cost completeness are separate. Three confirm cells and three pilot cells have partial usage; only 5/7 confirm B0/E1 pairs and 4/6 pilot pairs are cost-valid, while the recorded 7-pair and 6-pair deltas still reproduce the R2 numbers.
claims.harness: per-cell usage, witness summaries and paired task/replicate joins
claims.limitation: No imputation of missing usage; recorded and cost-valid tables are both reported. The valid confirm subset is task-type biased.

claims.claim: The user-supplied paired economics are reproduced exactly: pilot E1-B0 = +1 pass, -30 requests, -204,950 uncached input, +43,904 cache read, -25,577 output; confirm = 0, -28, +169,138, -186,496, -18,954.
claims.harness: six pilot pairs and seven confirm pairs from the immutable reports
claims.limitation: The numbers are recorded, not cost-complete; the cost-valid pair deltas differ in magnitude and are reported separately.

claims.claim: The old 54-cell confirm is explicitly terminated as a stress-lane result with 23 valid, 1 unresolved and 30 never-started cells; no further live calls will be spent on its non-product treatment. The partial evidence and corrected ledger are preserved.
claims.harness: the corrected unique-cell ledger and the product decision
claims.limitation: A decision not to complete a non-product treatment; it is not a claim about what the missing cells would have shown.

claims.claim: The R3 decision is no product candidate and Deployment Hold remains. The confirm is explicitly terminated as a stress-lane result, the paired pass difference is 0 in the confirm, the economics direction is unstable, cost validity is incomplete, and the stress lane is not a shipped preset.
claims.harness: the product-frontier report and the eligibility ledger
claims.limitation: A decision not to promote on current evidence; it is not a claim that E1 is ineffective.

claims.claim: The EF-R2 live evidence is archived incrementally: 548 files, 46,853,151 bytes, 43 raw attempts (18 pilot + 25 confirm attempts), 23 valid confirm cells, 2 transport-failed attempts and 30 never-started cells, with zero credentials found and a verified git bundle.
claims.harness: verbatim copy + SHA256SUMS + git bundle verify + credential scan
claims.limitation: The second copy is another local volume (E:), not an off-machine backup.

claims.claim: Both the primary archive and the E: copy match all 548 SHA256SUMS entries and the pointer; the scan found zero credentials.
claims.harness: eval/e2e/src/verify-archive.mjs against the repository pointer
claims.limitation: A local copy on a second volume, not an off-machine backup.

claims.claim: A 31-cell completion design is frozen for the 1 unresolved and 30 never-started cells, interleaved across T13-T16, pinned to the effective R2 config (hint 400), with a new manifest hash and executionAuthorized=false.
claims.harness: unique-cell ledger + R2 manifest + protocol amendment
claims.limitation: Design only. It requires a new explicit authorization and a passing representative transport health probe; unused R2 envelope capacity is not permission.

claims.claim: A 72-cell product-representative lane is designed with the shipped economy/balanced/quality configs and a proposed 32k first window; it has no frozen task set, no live data and executionAuthorized=false.
claims.harness: resolveEfConfig for the shipped presets + stress/product config diff
claims.limitation: Design only. The R2 tasks need an offline exposure audit at the proposed window, or new instances.

claims.claim: At 32k with the shipped economy values, all 16 audited seed surfaces cross the threshold and reach the fold path, and 16 commit at least one fold. The six pilot instances T11-p1 through T16-p1 each commit two folds with no refusal; the R2 T16 stress instances show a retry false admission.
claims.harness: keyless E2E host, seeded task histories, scripted summarizer, exact-span probe
claims.limitation: Exposure and the fold path only; the scripted summary is not a live model and task quality is not measured.

claims.claim: The exact-span admission candidate would refuse the 4 audited false admissions (all T16-s1/s2 retries) and has 0 false refusals in the audit. No default change is justified; the product pilot tests the shipped preset as-is.
claims.harness: the exposure audit probes; candidate = admission on the executed span
claims.limitation: A single compactIfNeeded call per surface with compactionRetries=1; a candidate refusal would take the rebase handoff, whose final pressure is not simulated.

claims.claim: The historical confirm and pilot each have 3 cost-invalid cells; the product pilot sets strictUsage=true and the runner stops with provider-usage-incomplete on any unknownUsage.
claims.harness: the unique-cell ledger, the product manifest, and the runner source
claims.limitation: The strict-usage rule is enforced for the product pilot; historical runs are not retroactively changed.

claims.claim: The 18-cell product-lane pilot executed 18/18 at 32k. B0 passed 5/6, E1 3/6 and E0 1/6; E1 had 0 task wins over B0 and B0 had 2. The EF arms were step-limited in 5/6 E0 and 3/6 E1 cells vs 0/6 B0. The decision is no product candidate, Deployment Hold, and do not expand to 72 cells.
claims.harness: native E2E host, six audited 32k tasks, three arms, one replicate; strict usage
claims.limitation: n=6 per arm; the EF quality comparison is censored by the 8-step harness limit, not a clean loss. One E1 cell has partial usage; one health-probe request exceeded the 60s p95 bound.

claims.claim: The pilot has 17/18 cost-valid cells. T16-p1-E1-r1 has one unknown usage out of 21 requests; strictUsage stopped the campaign after all 18 cells, so coverage is complete but the cost axis is incomplete for that cell and its B0/E1 pair.
claims.harness: per-cell usage and the strictUsage runner rule
claims.limitation: One cell; no imputation. The cost-valid paired subset is 5/6.

claims.claim: The representative health probe passed transport/usage 16/16 with zero transport errors, but one request took 82,290 ms and the p95 exceeded the pre-registered 60,000 ms bound. The pilot proceeded under a recorded latency deviation.
claims.harness: four long-payload profiles, four attempts each, local provider route
claims.limitation: A single local route and one outlier; latency is not certified and the probe is not a model-quality measurement.

claims.claim: The 18-cell product-lane pilot raw evidence is archived incrementally: 245 files, 37,802,090 bytes, 18 cells, 9 passes, 17 cost-valid cells, 8 step-limited cells; zero credentials, git bundle verified, primary and E: copies verified.
claims.harness: verbatim raw runs + evidence + git bundle + SHA256SUMS + credential scan
claims.limitation: The second copy is another local volume, not an off-machine backup.

claims.claim: The R3 offline closure made no provider request: at the time of the audit the only new run was a scripted self-test with 0 requests and no new results file. The later health probe and product pilot are separately authorized live steps.
claims.harness: baseline timestamp + new run/results directory audit at the offline closure
claims.limitation: A worktree audit of the offline phase, not a network capture. It does not cover the later authorized probe and pilot.

claims.claim: R3 started at 4affdee on chore/ef-c1-evaluation-foundation with a clean worktree (excluding ignored run output and eval/r3), PR #5 open and the supported CI lane green; all 22 immutable R2 artifacts are present and hashed.
claims.harness: git/gh metadata + SHA-256 inventory
claims.limitation: The PR and CI state are a snapshot at the start of R3.

note: The EF-R1 and EF-R2 registries are unchanged. A missing artifact is reported, never inferred.
